content.comment_body: Hello everyone, The firmware upgrade process using [product_name] (with display) is straightforward and allows you to monitor the update on the screen, indicating completion and status. However, I did not find details in the [product_name] manuals about firmware updates for [product_name] without display. Although I know the process is similar, how can I confirm the update has finished successfully without visual cues? Thanks in advance. [user_name]
You can check the firmware version via [product_name] software. Go to Tools > Transfer > Show FW Version.

My point is, with [product_name] with a display, you get a progress bar and confirmation message when updating firmware. Is there any way to observe update progress on [product_name] without display, like flashing LEDs or a RUN/STOP indicator? Thanks again.

For [product_name] modules without a display, there's no progress bar or message feedback. Since I don't have experience with updatable [product_name] modules without display, I'm unable to provide a direct answer. You might want to submit a support request for more information.

Firmware update process for [product_name] without display: - Power up the module using the included Micro SD card with the update file (no other files present). - The front LED will continuously flash during the update. - Once the update is complete, the LED remains steady.

analysis.insight_summary: Users upgrading firmware on [product_name] modules without displays are unsure how to monitor progress, as feedback differs from the display-equipped version. The documentation lacks clear information about indicators for these models. Eventually, it was clarified that the flashing LED indicates an ongoing update and turns constant on completion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a clear way to confirm firmware update progress and completion on [product_name] modules without display, similar to what is available on display models. They look for visual signals from the hardware (such as LEDs) or detailed documentation to guide them through the process.
